source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Offering fairly little meaningful benefit to clients or families managing chronic liver disease day to day","B":"Providing peer connection, shared coping strategies, and emotional support from others managing similar chronic liver disease challenges","C":"Applying mainly to clients currently on the liver transplant waiting list, rather than to clients with liver disease broadly","D":"Taking the place of the professional medical or psychological care the client and family would otherwise still need"}}
source_row.rationale: Liver disease support groups can provide valuable peer connection, shared coping strategies, and emotional support from others managing similar chronic liver disease challenges, a complementary resource alongside professional care, beneficial across the spectrum of liver disease severity, not only for transplant candidates.
source_row.source_detail: Value of Peer Support Groups in Liver Disease
source_row.source_name: American Liver Foundation — Support Group Resources
